paper.title_en: Maxwell-$\Lambda (x)$-supported regular black holes in unimodular gravity
paper.abstract_en: Recent results [1 ] show that, when the Einstein Equivalence Principle (EEP) is taken as a fundamental postulate in vacuum, the resulting geometric constraints lead to the condition $g=-1$, corresponding to the spacetime volume element of the Minkowski vacuum. This provides a motivation for considering the unimodular framework, in which the cosmological constant arises as an integration constant in the conservative case and can be generalized to a spacetime-dependent integration function $\Lambda (x)$ when energy-momentum conservation is relaxed. Within this setting, regular black-hole geometries can be supported by significantly simpler matter sources, as part of the effective stress-energy tensor is absorbed into a spacetime-dependent vacuum contribution $\Lambda (r)$, allowing for Maxwell realizations in a broad class of cases. A global Maxwell description exists if and only if a geometric function H(r) remains non-negative; violations of this condition signal the necessity of a nonlinear electromagnetic sector in part of the spacetime. These results suggest that, within the phenomenological non-conservative unimodular framework considered here, black-hole regularization can be partially reinterpreted as an interplay between the electromagnetic and spacetime-dependent $\Lambda (r)$ sectors.
